page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v6 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft's ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical CPU cores operating at 3.4 GHz with 1 thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 96 GB of RAM, equating to a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 2,832 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. It operates without hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight superior multi-threaded compute and data-transfer throughput. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 22,029 and a strong stress-ng multi-core score of 99,380.68. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 464.03 GB/sec and write bandwidth measures 200.4 GB/sec, placing memory subsystems in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Conversely, single-core execution remains in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, reflecting a focus on dense multi-core scaling rather than peak single-threaded frequency.

With 2,832 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity and top-tier PassMark database operation scores (37,498.13), this instance provides strong resource density and input-output capabilities. It delivers high throughput for static web serving (74.8 GB/sec) and Redis operations (89.96 million SET ops/sec). The 2 GB per core memory profile represents a trade-off, restricting memory-heavy enterprise jobs, but optimizing compute efficiency for high-concurrency software builds, caching tiers, data transformation, and distributed web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by 48 dedicated 3.4 GHz ARM Neoverse-N2 cores, 96 GB of system memory, and 2,832 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation emphasizes compute density over large memory footprints. In benchmark testing, the instance excels in parallel computing and data transit, recording top-tier Geekbench multi-core results, uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 464 GB/sec, and high-performance database execution. While single-thread execution sits in the median range and large-model inference shows predictable latency tradeoffs without GPU acceleration, its multi-core efficiency and fast bundled storage make it an effective platform for multi-threaded compilation, high-throughput web serving, containerized microservices, and fast caching layers such as Redis.
